marks.gloss_en: נצא -- הא דאמרן; בר נצא -- דכתיב וירב בנחל
this is what is written: 'and the son of Jonathan was Meriv-Baal' (I Chr 8:34) -- was Meriv-Baal his name? was not Mefiboshet his name? rather, because he made a quarrel with his Master
he said to him: I said 'when will you come in peace', and you do this to me? Not against you do I have grievances but against Him who brought you in peace
when David said to Mefiboshet 'you and Ziba shall divide the field', a bat kol went out and said to him: Rehoboam and Jeroboam shall divide the kingdom
had David not accepted slander, the kingdom of the house of David would not have been divided

מקיש ראשונים לאחרונים: מה אחרונים לא עשו ותלה בהן לשבח, אף ראשונים לא עשו ותלה בהן לגנאי -- as Scripture credits Josiah with destroying what he did not destroy, so it charges Solomon with building what he did not build
והלא כל עבודה זרה שבארץ ישראל אסא ויהושפט ביערום -- so the later king did not do what the verse credits him with

R' Yosei: is it possible that Asa came and did not destroy them, Jehoshaphat and did not destroy them, until Josiah came and destroyed them? surely Asa and Jehoshaphat destroyed all the idolatry in the Land of Israel
שנאמר ולא היה לבבו שלם... כלבב דוד אביו -- כלבב דוד אביו הוא דלא הוה, מיחטא נמי לא חטא
whoever says Solomon sinned is simply mistaken
the verse names Solomon as builder of the high places that Josiah defiled
אלא כדתניא, רבי יוסי אומר... אף ראשונים לא עשו ותלה בהן לגנאי -- the 'building' is Scripture's charge, not Solomon's act
אלא כדתניא, רבי יוסי אומר -- Solomon did not build them; Scripture hangs the building on him for disgrace, as it hangs the destruction on Josiah for praise (hekesh_rishonim_laacharonim)

R' Yosei: 'and the high places before Jerusalem, at the right of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon king of Israel built for Ashtoret the abomination of the Sidonians...' (II Kings 23:13) [the verse continues: the king (Josiah) defiled]
אלא מה אני מקיים ויהי לעת זקנת שלמה נשיו הטו את לבבו -- the verse (I Kings 11:4) says his wives turned his heart
ההיא כרבי נתן -- they turned his heart to go after other gods, and he did not go (= p_nashav_hitu_velo_halach)

R' Natan set 'and in Solomon's old age his wives turned his heart' against 'as the heart of David his father' (he did not sin), and resolved: this is what it says -- his wives turned his heart to go after other gods, and he did not go
והכתיב אז יבנה שלמה במה לכמוש שקוץ מואב -- 'then Solomon built a high place for Kemosh' (I Kings 11:7)
'then Solomon built (יבנה)' means he sought to build and did not build
אלא מעתה: אז יבנה יהושע מזבח לה' -- שביקש לבנות ולא בנה?! אלא דבנה, הכא נמי דבנה -- 'then Joshua built an altar' (Josh 8:30) uses the same form and means he built; so here too he built
והכתיב ויעש שלמה הרע בעיני ה' -- 'and Solomon did evil in the Lord's eyes' (I Kings 11:6)
אלא מפני שהיה לו למחות בנשיו ולא מיחה, מעלה עליו הכתוב כאילו חטא -- since he should have protested against his wives and did not, Scripture counts it against him as if he sinned
it would be better for that righteous man to be a servant to 'another thing', and that 'and he did evil in the Lord's eyes' not be written of him

when Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter she brought him a thousand kinds of music and said to him 'thus one does for such-and-such idol, and thus for such-and-such idol', and he did not protest against her
when Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter Gabriel descended and stuck a reed in the sea, a sandbank rose up on it, and on it was built a great city [of Rome]
on the day Jeroboam brought in the two golden calves, one in Bethel and one in Dan, a single hut was built, and that is Italy of Greece
שנאמר ויעש הישר בעיני ה' וילך בכל דרך דוד אביו
אלא מה אני מקיים וכמהו לא היה לפניו מלך אשר שב וגו' -- the verse (II Kings 23:25) says he 'returned' to the Lord
whoever says Josiah sinned is simply mistaken
שמא תאמר נטל מזה ונתן לזה -- תלמוד לומר בכל מאדו: שנתן להם משלו
every judgment he judged from eight to eighteen he returned to them, from his own money (= p_shav_hechziran, p_meodo_natan_mishelo)
[the 'returning' of II Kings 23:25 is that] every judgment he judged from [age] eight to eighteen he returned to them
דאמר מר: רבי אבא ואחא אחי הוו -- hence 'Acha, brother of Abba'
there is none greater among penitents than Josiah in his generation
Rav Yosef: and another one in our generation
